overall_validity.rationale: All modeled variables and rules are instantiated in a way that closely matches their formal definitions: the agent’s role and behavior consistently reflect short-run profit maximization under limited but actively used coercive powers, in a setting of frequent disputes, low and slowly moving reputation, highly aggressive users, concentrated power in a few institutional actors, and large net payoffs to aggressive tactics under a lenient, stochastic sanction regime. World updates (context, resources, actors) evolve round by round in line with specified frequencies and constraints, and the consequence structure explicitly implements the intended risk–return logic, including high revenue from aggressive/coercive responses and only rare, minor compliance deductions. Rendering instructions are followed carefully: every round includes consequence, context/resource/actor updates, antecedents, and responses; no extraneous confounds or meta-level references are introduced; and hostility, power, and volatility are shown through concrete events and messages rather than declarative labels. Because any minor imperfections, if present, would be peripheral and do not materially affect the core causal pathways being tested (e.g., how lenient sanctions and high aggression payoff shape the agent’s sustained aggressive behavior), the simulation provides a robust and uncontaminated test of the targeted behavioral dynamics.
